newsitem.title: UK: Signet hopes for green light on capital plan.
newsitem.headline: Signet hopes for green light on capital plan.

text.p: Jewellery retailer Signet Group Plc said on Wednesday it was optimistic its proposed capital restructuring stood a good chance of getting shareholder approval.
Chairman James McAdam said the company's plans to convert all classes of preference shares into new ordinary shares, were pitched at a level which the board considered acceptable to all shareholders.
"This represents what we think will have the best chance of success," McAdam told a news conference.

The restructuring, which will ask shareholders to forego 164.5 million stg in dividend arrears, includes the elimination of a 199 million deficit on the firm's profit and loss account. This will pave the way for resumption of dividend payments at some stage.
McAdam said, however, it was most unlikely the group, which suspended dividend payments in January 1992, would pay a dividend in 1997/98.

Under the proposal Signet, the former Ratners jewellery chain, will give preference shareholders 82.5 percent of its new ordinary share capital, while existing ordinary shareholders will have 17.5 percent.
Julian Treger of UK Active Value Fund, a Signet preference shareholder which has long been pressing for a capital shake-up, said he welcomed the restructuring.
"We've been waiting for a long time for this," he said by telephone, "We welcome it, it will increase the value of the company significantly."

Earlier this year Signet also signed a new three-year credit facility for $360 million with a syndicate of four banks. At the end of the year to February 1 1997 its net debt was 240.2 million stg, down 22 percent.
The group also announced an 80 percent increase in pretax profits to 45.1 million stg.

McAdam said none of the group's businesses were up for sale. Last year Signet's UK businesses were the subject of an offer from a venture capitalist group and preference shareholders in the past had pressed for the group to be broken up.
The company owns Ernest Jones and H. Samuel chains in Britain as well as major jewellery stores in the United States. Its shares closed at 5.75 pence lower at 30.75 pence.
